1. WAS ANY II.3 MEANING LOST IN THE TRANSLATION? FOUR, NAMED WITH THEIR SENTENCE, AND THE FIRST IS THE SHARP ONE.

(i) VERSIONING. The CONTRACTS preamble at the pin reads 'Source: brief II.3, eleven contracts, proposed canonical, versioned.' ZERO OF ELEVEN schemas carry a contract-version property. $id carries a NAME, not a version. The gap is not hypothetical: RenderPackage's own item 1 is 'supported contract/template versions', so the counterpart is specified to negotiate against a version that the other ten contracts do not expose. I did NOT add one, because the order's BOUNDS say a property with no source line in the CONTRACTS table or the semantics paragraph is a fabrication, and no row's required-meaning column names a version. So it is NAMED rather than filled: this is a table-row edit or a PRD addendum, an issuer's cut, not a worker's widening. If the CVO or the CTO wants it, one field (`contract_version`, required, on all eleven) closes it and every fixture moves with it.

(ii) 'Server-only credential and vendor-routing fields never reach the browser' (CONTRACTS preamble). A JSON Schema is a SHAPE, not a transport rule. FOUR sites carry the marker -- ResolvedScope.vendor_ids (x-server-only), AnalysisReport.release.protected_pdf_ref.server_only (const true), ExportReceipt.artifact (x-server-only + server_only const true), StatusEnvelope.internal_correlation_id (x-server-only) -- and NOTHING validates that a response actually omitted them, because a validator sees the document it is handed, not the one that crossed the wire. The guarantee has to live in the serializing handler and in B3's reauthorize-before-serve. The marker makes the intent machine-READABLE for that handler; it does not make it machine-CHECKED, and the difference should be read as a debt on IB-s-3 and IB-s-15, not as a property of these schemas.

(iii) 'A change needs matching producer and consumer fixtures' (CONTRACTS preamble). Every contract ships a PRODUCER-side pair here. Nothing binds a CHANGE to a matching CONSUMER fixture, and the consumer is a DIFFERENT PROJECT (IRPT_FNTEND). Recorded in the code home's README as a rule; there is no gate, and I did not build one -- an agent-made gate nobody asked for is its own defect.

(iv) PerformanceReport item 5, 'optional benchmark/value facts only when supported'. The schema carries benchmark, value_facts and supported, but does NOT enforce the CONDITIONAL: an instance with supported:false and a populated benchmark object VALIDATES today. A draft-2020-12 if/then would close it. I left it open because 'only when supported' admits two readings (supported by the PROVIDER, or supported for THIS request) and picking one silently would have been the wrong kind of decision at a scaffolding cell; it belongs to B11 (IB-s-11), which is where the provider capability is actually known.

PARTIALLY carried, worth one line: ExportBundle's consumer column reads 'B14 render; FNTEND F8 (preview -- a preview never calls the vendor again)'. The const false covers RENDER. The word PREVIEW names an FE surface this contract cannot reach, so the render half is enforced and the preview half is carried only as prose.

The 21 MEASURED are exactly the entries whose owner the PRD states in its own words, quoted per entry in owner_source: IRPT_BCKEND 11 (the three new homes, the seven proposed opal-data-ycharts layout tokens, the /api/scoped/investor-reporting/... route), NEWS PRODUCERS 6 (the three news Lambdas and the three news data resources), EXISTING SECRET OWNERS 4 (the four Secrets Manager names). The other 53 carry owner_project 'EXISTING-UNNAMED-IN-PRD' with owner_claim 'absent', because the PRD's ONLY statement about them is 'their existing owners' -- and an invented project name in an owner field is worse than an honest absence, since a consumer cannot reject what looks authoritative. In place of the invention each entry carries a MEASURED commit-plane lane from the estate's own resolver: ANY 17, CLOUD_OPS_OR_ETL 15, POD4 5, POD1_OR_AE 4, DECK 4, ANY_CTO 2, BASE_EXEC 1, POD4_OR_AE 1, YCHARTS_PULL_MODULE 1 (50 of 74); the remaining 24 have no lane because they are not repo paths (15) or sit inside the unchecked-out portal submodule (9).

THREE THINGS A GRADER SHOULD TEST RATHER THAN TAKE FROM ME. (a) A LANE IS THE COMMIT-PLANE OWNER, NOT THE OPERATIONAL ONE. data/firm_registry.json resolves to lane ANY, which is true of who may commit it and says NOTHING about who maintains its content; if 'owner' is meant to name who answers for the DATA, then 53 of 74 entries are honestly blank and the register, not the manifest, is where that question lands. (b) THE INSTRUMENT IS WORKTREE-SHAPED. resolve_lane read .owned-paths.yaml BY PATH from this worktree, not from HEAD; the file is unmodified here (git status clean on it), so worktree == 261c8d2080, but the reading would drift silently on a tree where it was edited. (c) ONE ROW I SPLIT AND A GRADER MIGHT NOT. PATHS row 23 (the three news Lambdas) is owned by NEWS PRODUCERS because the PRD's use column says 'news production; ownership stays with its producers'; row 24 (portal_data_proxy, the trending publisher, four portal/src/api files) I left EXISTING-UNNAMED because its use column names 'current serving boundaries' and the SURFACE MANIFEST assigns the news producers the TABLES and the BUCKET, not the serving path. A grader who reads row 24 as news-owned moves 6 entries from absent to measured. I state the reading rather than hide it inside a count.

3. WHICH PROPERTIES DID I SHAPE BY JUDGMENT -- AND FIRST, THE BLIND SPOT THAT CHANGES HOW TO READ THE LIST. Arm (a)'s backward control proves 384 of 384 description quotes RESOLVE in the CONTRACTS section. IT DOES NOT PROVE THE PROPERTY WAS NAMED BY THE ITEM IT CITES. A property whose EXISTENCE I derived from the endpoint, from a cell's acceptance clause or from CLAUDE.md, and which then cites the nearest table item, passes that control cleanly. So what follows is not what the battery found; it is precisely what the battery CANNOT see, enumerated by its author. Denominator: 361 named properties across the eleven schemas.

(1) DirectoryEntry item 4, 'termination indicator SEPARATE from access', admits two shapes: two sibling carriers, or one field plus a rule. I built TWO -- `termination` {indicator, effective_date} and `access` {entitled, reason} -- and the VALID fixture is a TERMINATED client with access GRANTED, so the separation is exercised rather than asserted. A reader who wanted one field with a derived flag gets a different wire shape from the same sentence.

(2) THE COHORT MAPPING, and it is the one I would most like a second reader on. The semantics paragraph says 'Opal Supervised/Unsupervised as fee-taking status; Advised/Residual as advisory status' and separately calls supervision and billing INDEPENDENT concepts. I named the fields by the GLOSS (`fee_taking_status`, `advisory_status`) rather than by the LABEL (`supervision_status`, ...). Same three enums, different keys, wire-visible, and NO fixture would notice the difference. B1 and B12 are where it becomes real.

(3) PerformanceReport.measurement_basis.`return_units` is a SIXTH field under a five-item source ('currency/method/fee/accrual/annualization'). I added it because item 4's returns are otherwise bare numbers and the endpoint's own constraint is that units are part of a number's meaning. It cites item 3; item 3 does not name it.

(4) THE SAME SHAPE, ENUMERATED SO IT IS COUNTABLE: TEN further properties exist because a DIFFERENT PRD section or a standing rule demanded them, each citing the nearest II.3 item -- AnalysisRequest.sender_evidence.display_from_used (B6's 'verified through the forwarding arrangement, not display From'); NarrativePacket.events[].series_basis and prose.states_contemporaneity and prose.asserts_causation (B13's acceptance and the endpoint's 'states contemporaneity and never causes'); HoldingsSnapshot.custody_totals.deduplicated (B12's 'parallel custody facts never unioned'); HoldingsSnapshot.nodes[].provenance.claim, whose enum is measured/inferred/held/absent from CLAUDE.md's A VALUE MUST CARRY ITS CLAIM and from NO PRD line at all; DirectoryEntry.revision.source_completion_date and .as_of_business_date (B1's 'as-of and source completion date carried on every entry'); PerformanceReport.returns.summary_returns[].absent_reason (B11's 'missing facts stay absent with reasons'); AnalysisRequest.identity.immutable. ELEVEN properties in total with (3). Every one is defensible and none is named by its cited item; a grader holding the BOUNDS strictly would strike them, and the schemas would then carry LESS than the estate's own rules require. That tension is the finding, not the fields.

(5) HoldingsSnapshot's eleven items describe a NODE and a SNAPSHOT without saying which is which. I put items 4-9 and 11 (hierarchy, namespaced ids, basis, amount+denominator, percentages, provenance, drill refs) on the node and items 1-3 and 10 (scope+source-set revision, clocks, unique custody totals, coverage/remainders) on the snapshot. 'coverage/remainders' as snapshot-level and 'drill refs' as node-level are both readable the other way.

(6) ResolvedScope item 5: I made `partial_reason` REQUIRED and NULLABLE rather than optional, so a producer must DECIDE rather than omit. The table says neither.

(7) ENUM MEMBERSHIPS ARE THE HIGHEST-TRAFFIC JUDGMENT IN THIS DELIVERABLE. Only StatusEnvelope's nine states are enumerated BY the table ('queued/running/ready/partial/stale/unavailable/needs-correction/uncertain/failed', carried verbatim and exhaustively). EVERY other enum here is mine, drawn from the PRD's cell rows and the endpoint's language: principal_class, scope_kind, identifier_namespace, node_kind, provider, basis, event_type, admission, job_state, validation_status and the rest. They are the cheapest thing in this deliverable to correct and the most likely to be wrong, and the first cell that PRODUCES an instance of each contract is where each one should be re-read.

mutant.description: The load-bearing claims are that the eleven schemas carry the table's meanings and invent nothing, that the manifest covers every PATHS token, that nine roots carry nine distinct keys and no state, and that the register carries Part V with owners. FOUR control layers, in the order they run. (1) THE BACKWARD ANTI-FABRICATION CONTROL, arm (a): forward coverage alone cannot see an INVENTED property, so every quoted span in every description must resolve VERBATIM in the CONTRACTS section at the pin -- 384 of 384. (2) THE DIFFERENCE CONTROL, arm (b): a valid fixture that validates proves nothing on its own (a schema of `{}` would pass it), so each contract also ships an INVALID fixture aimed at that contract's own hazard, and a schema whose invalid fixture passes FAILS the arm. (3) THE COVERAGE ARM READS THE RAW TOKEN, arm (c): matching on the manifest's own RESOLVED path would let one resolution bug pass both sides, so coverage is matched on the raw PRD token and the resolutions are verified separately against git. (4) RED-FIRST MUTANTS ON THE BATTERY ITSELF, because a declared falsifier that never ran is a promise: SIX mutants, one or two per arm, each applied to the real deliverable, measured, then restored and the restore verified by sha256. NAMED HONESTLY: the FIRST attempt at the arm-(a) mutant was a NO-OP -- it searched the raw JSON text for an unescaped double quote and matched nothing, so the battery correctly printed the token and the control read as a FAILURE TO FIRE. A no-op mutant and a blind detector are indistinguishable from the outside; it was diagnosed and re-run JSON-aware, and both arm-(a) mutants then fired.
